On moving down the group electron gain enthalpy decreases. Oxygen due to its small size causes electron-electron repulsions in relatively small \(2 p\)-subshell. 6222.text:
Which statement among the following is true?
(i) The function $f ( x ) = x | x |$ is strictly increasing on $R - { 0 }$.
(ii) The function $f ( x ) = {\log}_{( 1 / 4 )}x$ is strictly increasing on $( 0, \infty )$.
(iii) A one-one function is always an increasing function.
(iv) $f ( x ) = {x}^{1 / 3}$ is strictly decreasing on $R$
6222.sol:
$\left(i\right)$ Given that $f\left(x\right) = x\left|x\right|$

Differentiate on both sides

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = x\dfrac{\left|x\right|}{x} + \left|x\right|$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2\left|x\right|$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) > 0 ∀ x \in R - \left\{0\right\}$

So $f\left(x\right)$ is strictly increasing function.

So it's true.

$\left(ii\right)$ $f\left(x\right) = log\dfrac{1}{4}\left(x\right)$

Differentiating on both sides

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{xlog\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)} = - \dfrac{1}{xlog\left(4\right)}$

$⇒ f ' \left(x\right) < 0 ∀ x \in \left(0, \infty\right)$

So it's false.

$\left(iii\right)$ A one-one function can be either increasing or decreasing but can not be always increasing function.

$\left(iv\right)f\left(x\right) = x\dfrac{1}{3}$

Differentiating on both sides

$f ' \left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{- 2}{3}$

$⇒ f ' \left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{3{\left[{x}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\right]}^{2}} > 0 ∀ x \in R$

So it's always increasing function .

Let, $B_1=$ Bags of first group, $B_2=$ Bags of second group
$P\left(B_1\right)=\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3}, P\left(B_2\right)=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}$
and let $B=$ the event that the ball is black
$P\left(\frac{B}{B_1}\right)=\frac{5}{8}, P\left(\frac{B}{B_2}\right)=\frac{2}{5}$
Now, $P\left(\frac{B_1}{B}\right)=\frac{P\left(B_1\right) P\left(\frac{B}{B_1}\right)}{P\left(B_1\right) P\left(\frac{B}{B_1}\right)+P\left(B_2\right) P\left(\frac{B}{B_2}\right)}=\frac{\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{8}}{\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{8}+\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{5}}=\frac{\frac{5}{8}}{\frac{5}{8}+\frac{4}{5}}=\frac{25}{57}$

11314.sol:
Let roots of equation be $2 \alpha, \alpha, \beta$
So, $3 \alpha+\beta=0 \Rightarrow \beta=-3 \alpha$ and $2 \alpha^2 \beta=\frac{-c}{a} \Rightarrow-6 \alpha^3=\frac{-c}{a} \Rightarrow \alpha^3=\frac{c}{6 a}$
Now, $a\left(\frac{c}{6 a}\right)+b\left(\frac{c}{6 a}\right)^{1 / 3}+c=0\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow b\left(\frac{c}{6 a}\right)^{1 / 3}=\frac{-c}{6}-c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{b^3 c}{6 a}=\frac{-343 c^3}{36 \times 6} \Rightarrow 36 b^3+343 c^2 a=0
\end{aligned}$

14596.subject: Physics
14596.text:
Two balls of charge $q_1$ and $q_2$ initially have a velocity of the same magnitude and direction. After a uniform electric field has been applied during a certain time, the direction of the velocity of the first ball changes by $60^{{}^{\circ}}$, and the velocity magnitude is reduced by half. The direction of the velocity of the second ball changes thereby by $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.
In what proportion will the velocity of the second ball change? Determine the magnitude of the charge-to-mass ratio for the second ball if it is equal to $k_1$ for the first ball. The electrostatic interaction between the balls should be neglected.
14596.sol:
Let $v_1$ and $v_2$ be the velocities of the first and second balls after the removal of the uniform electric field. By hypothesis, the angle between the velocity $v_1$ and the initial velocity $v$ is $60^{{}^{\circ}}$. Therefore, the change in the momentum of the first ball is $\Delta$ p_1=q_1 E $\Delta$ t=m_1 v \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}} Here we use the condition that $ v_1=v / 2$, which implies that the change in the momentum $\Delta \mathrm{p}_1$ of the first ball occurs in a direction perpendicular to the direction of its velocity $v_1$.
Since $\mathrm{E} \| \Delta \mathrm{p}_1$ and the direction of variation of the second ball momentum is parallel to the direction of $\Delta p_1$, we obtain for the velocity of the second ball (it can easily be seen that the charges on the balls have the same sign) v_2=v \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}}=$\frac{v}{\sqrt{3}}$ The corresponding change in the momentum of the second ball is $\Delta$ p_2=q_2 E $\Delta$ t=$\frac{m_2 v}{\cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}}$ Hence we obtain $\begin{aligned}& \frac{q_1}{q_2}=\frac{m_1 \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}}{m_2 / \cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}},\\
& \frac{q_2}{m_2}=\frac{4}{3} \frac{q_1}{m_1}=\frac{4}{3} k_1 .
\end{aligned}
$

20342.text:
Match the names of reactions given in Column I with the appropriate reactions given in Column II. <
No.Name of reactionNo.Equations representing reactions
ASandmeyerP$2C_6H_5Cl + Na$ (dry ether) \to Diphenyl
BFittigQ$ CH_3 - CHBr - CH_3 + AgF \to CH_3 - CHF - CH_3 + AgBr$
CSwartsR$CH_3 - CH_2 - Br + NaI$ (Acetone) $\to CH_3 - CH_2 - I + NaBr$
DFinkelsteinS$C_6H_5N_2^+ Cl^- + Cu_2Br_2/HBr \to C_6H_5Br + N_2$
20342.sol:
Sandmeyer reaction involves the conversion of diazonium salts to aryl halides using copper(I) salts. This corresponds to reaction (S): $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{ N}_2^{+} \mathrm{Cl}^{-} + \mathrm{Cu}_2 \mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{HBr} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{N}_2$.

Fittig reaction involves the coupling of two aryl halides in the presence of sodium metal in dry ether to form diphenyl. This corresponds to reaction (P): $2 \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{Na} \text{ (dry ether) } \rightarrow \text{Diphenyl}$.

Swarts reaction is used for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides from alkyl halides using metallic fluorides like $\mathrm{AgF}$. This corresponds to reaction (Q): $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}_3 + \mathrm{AgF} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CHF}-\mathrm{CH}_3 + \mathrm{AgBr}$.

Finkelstein reaction involves the exchange of halogen atoms (usually chlorine or bromine) with iodine in the presence of sodium iodide in acetone. This corresponds to reaction (R): $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{NaI} \text{ (Acetone) } \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{I} + \mathrm{NaBr}$.

Thus, the correct matching is A=S, B=P, C=Q, D=R.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{R}$

21613.text: $\sin ^{-1}(x-1)+\cos ^{-1}(x-3)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2-x^2}\right)=\cos ^{-1} k+\pi$, then the value of ' $k$ ' is
21613.sol:
The domain of $\sin^{-1}(x-1)$ is $-1 \le x-1 \le 1$, which implies $0 \le x \le 2$.

Substituting $x = 2$ into the given equation:

$\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \pi + \tan^{-1}(-1) = \cos^{-1} k + \pi$

$\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \cos^{-1} k$

$\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \cos^{-1} k$

$k = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

22958.text: The average energy associated with a monoatomic molecule is
22958.sol:
A monoatomic gas molecule has 3 degrees of freedom ($f = 3$) corresponding to its translational motion along the $x$, $y$, and $z$ axes.

According to the law of equipartition of energy, each degree of freedom contributes $\dfrac{1}{2} K_{B} T$ to the average kinetic energy of the molecule.

Therefore, the total average energy $E$ is given by $E = f \times \dfrac{1}{2} K_{B} T = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{2} K_{B} T = \dfrac{3}{2} K_{B} T$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2} K_{B} T$

23017.subject: Physics
23017.text: A charged particle is released from rest in a region of space in which steady and uniform electric and magnetic fields are parallel to each other. The particle will move in a
23017.sol:
The force on a charged particle moving in electric and magnetic fields is given by the Lorentz force equation: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

Given that the electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ are parallel, let $\vec{E} = E\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = B\hat{k}$. The particle is released from rest, so its initial velocity $\vec{v} = 0$.

The initial force acting on the particle is $\vec{F} = q\vec{E} = qE\hat{k}$. This force causes the particle to accelerate in the direction of the electric field, which is along the $\hat{k}$ axis.

As the particle gains velocity $\vec{v}$ in the $\hat{k}$ direction, the magnetic force $\vec{F}_m = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ is calculated. Since $\vec{v}$ is parallel to $\vec{B}$, the cross product $\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = 0$.

Consequently, the magnetic force remains zero throughout the motion. The particle continues to experience only the electric force $qE$ in the direction of the electric field. Since the initial velocity is zero and the net force is always parallel to the initial displacement, the particle moves in a straight line.

Answer: Straight line

23583.subject: Physics
23583.text: In an adiabatic process with the ratio of two specific heat, $\gamma=\dfrac{3}{2}$, pressure is increased by $\dfrac{2}{3} \%$, then decrease in the volume will be
23583.sol:
For an adiabatic process, the relation between pressure $P$ and volume $V$ is given by $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides, we get $\ln P + \gamma \ln V = \text{constant}$.

Differentiating both sides, we obtain $\dfrac{dP}{P} + \gamma \dfrac{dV}{V} = 0$, which implies $\dfrac{dV}{V} = -\dfrac{1}{\gamma} \dfrac{dP}{P}$.

Given $\gamma = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and the percentage increase in pressure $\dfrac{dP}{P} = \dfrac{2}{3} \%$.

Substituting these values, the percentage change in volume is $\dfrac{dV}{V} = -\dfrac{1}{3/2} \times \dfrac{2}{3} \% = -\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} \% = -\dfrac{4}{9} \%$.

The negative sign indicates a decrease in volume. Therefore, the decrease in volume is $\dfrac{4}{9} \%$.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{9} \%$

$= 0 . 36 \times {10}^{– 10}F$

Capacitance for the lower part can be written as,

${C}_{2} = \dfrac{K{A}_{2}{ε}_{0}}{d} = \dfrac{3 \times \left(0 . 10 \times 0 . 5\right) \times \left(9 \times {10}^{- 12}\right)}{5 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

$⇒ {C}_{2} = 0 . 27 \times {10}^{– 10}F$

Both part of the capacitor can be considered as connected in parallel,

${C}_{eff} = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2}$

$= 63pF$

26098.text: Shown in the figure is a semicircular metallic strip that has thickness $t$ and resistivity $ρ$. Its inner radius is ${R}_{1}$ and outer radius is ${R}_{2}$. If a voltage ${V}_{0}$ is applied between its two ends, a current $I$ flows in it. In addition, it is observed that a transverse voltage $\DeltaV$ develops between its inner and outer surfaces due to purely kinetic effects of moving electrons (ignore any role of the magnetic field due to the current). Then (figure is schematic and not drawn to scale)
options: the outer surface is at a higher voltage than the inner surface
the outer surface is at a lower voltage than the inner surface
26098.sol:
Resistance of the strip $= ρ\dfrac{\pir}{tdr}$

$R =$net resistance

$\dfrac{1}{R} = ∫ \dfrac{tdr}{ρ\pir}\dfrac{t}{\piρ}{∫}_{{R}_{1}}^{{R}_{2}}\dfrac{dr}{r}$

$R = \dfrac{\piρ}{tln\left(\dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}}\right)}$

Hence, current i $= \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{R} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}t}{\piρ}ln\left(\dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}}\right)$

for elementary dr,

$di = \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{ρ\left(\dfrac{\pir}{tdr}\right)} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}tdr}{ρ\pir}$

$i = nAev$

$\dfrac{{V}_{0}tdr}{ρ\pir} = nt\left(dr\right)ev$

$eE = m\dfrac{{v}^{2}}{r} = m{V}_{0}^{2}{n}^{2}{ℓ}^{2}{ρ}^{2}{\pi}^{2}{r}^{2} \times \dfrac{1}{r}$

$m\dfrac{{v}^{2}}{r} = m{V}_{0}^{2}{n}^{2}{ℓ}^{2}{ρ}^{2}{\pi}^{2}{r}^{2} \times \dfrac{1}{r}$

$E ∝ \dfrac{1}{{r}^{3}}$

$E = k\dfrac{1}{{r}^{3}}$

$\DeltaV = ∫ Edr = k{∫}_{{R}_{1}}^{{R}_{2}}\dfrac{dr}{{r}^{2}} ∝ {V}_{0}^{2}$

$∴ ∝ {i}^{2}$

33619.text: A point $P$ moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points $\left(1, 2\right) and \left(- 2, 1\right) is $14$. Let $f$\left(x, y\right)$ = 0$ be the locus of $P$, which intersects the $x$-axis at the points A, B$ and the $y$-axis at the point $C, D$. Then the area of the quadrilateral $ACBD$ is equal to
33619.sol:
Given,

A point $P$ moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points $\left(1, 2\right)$ and $\left(- 2, 1\right)$ is $14$.

So, ${\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2} = 14$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + x - 3y - 2 = 0$

Put $x = 0$

$⇒ {y}^{2} - 3y - 2 = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}$

Put $y = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + x - 2 = 0$

$\left(x + 2\right)\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$∴ A\left(- 2, 0\right), B\left(1, 0\right), C\left(0, \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2}\right), D\left(0, \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\right)$

Area formed by $ACBD$ will be $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2} \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2} \\ - 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|- 3 - \sqrt{17} - \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{2} + 3 - \sqrt{17}\right|$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times \sqrt{17} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{17}}{2}$ sq units.

33750.subject: Mathematics
33750.text: Let $z$ be a complex number such that $|z+2| = |z-2|$ and $\arg\left(\dfrac{z+3}{z-i}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Then $|z|^2$ is equal to:
33750.sol:
Given $|z+2| = |z-2|$, the point $z$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining $(-2, 0)$ and $(2, 0)$. This means $z$ lies on the imaginary axis.

Let $z = iy$, where $y \in \mathbb{R}$.

We are given $\arg\left(\dfrac{z+3}{z-i}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Substituting $z = iy$, we get:

$\dfrac{iy+3}{iy-i} = \dfrac{3+iy}{i(y-1)} = \dfrac{-i(3+iy)}{y-1} = \dfrac{y - 3i}{y-1} = \dfrac{y}{y-1} - i\dfrac{3}{y-1}$

For a complex number $X + iY$ to have an argument of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, its real and imaginary parts must be equal and strictly positive. Therefore:

$\dfrac{y}{y-1} = \dfrac{-3}{y-1} > 0$

Since $y \neq 1$, equating the numerators gives $y = -3$.

Checking for positivity: $\dfrac{-3}{-3-1} = \dfrac{3}{4} > 0$, which is valid.

Thus, $z = -3i$.

The value of $|z|^2$ is $|-3i|^2 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

If the system of linear equations
$7x + 11y + \alphaz = 13$
$5x + 4y + 7z = \beta$
$175x + 194y + 57z = 361$

34481.sol:
Given,

System of linear equations,

$7x + 11y + \alphaz = 13$
$5x + 4y + 7z = \beta$
$175x + 194y + 57z = 361$

Now we know that, for infinite solution $D = {D}_{1} = {D}_{2} = {D}_{3} = 0$

Now solving $D = 0$ we get,

$\left|\begin{cases}7 & 11 & \alpha \\ 5 & 4 & 7 \\ 175 & 194 & 57\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Now applying operation ${R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - 25{R}_{1}$ we get,

$\left|\begin{cases}7 & 11 & \alpha \\ 5 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & - 81 & 57 - 25\alpha\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 81 ( 49 - 5\alpha ) + ( 57 - 25\alpha ) ( - 27 ) = 0$

$⇒ 270\alpha = - 2430 ⇒ \alpha = - 9$

And now solving ${D}_{1} = 0$ we get,

$\left|\begin{cases}13 & 11 & - 9 \\ \beta & 4 & 7 \\ 361 & 194 & 57\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 13\left(4 \times 57 - 7 \times 194\right) - \beta\left(11 \times 57 + 9 \times 194\right) + 361\left(11 \times 7 + 9 \times 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ 13\left(- 1130\right) - \beta\left(2373\right) + 361\left(113\right) = 0$

$⇒ 13\left(- 10\right) - \beta\left(21\right) + 361 = 0$

$⇒ 21\beta = 231$

$⇒ \beta = 11$

$∴ \alpha + \beta + 2 = 4$

34751.text: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}y}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x} = x{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}, 0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ with $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{32}$. If $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\left(\alpha\right)}$, then the value of $3{\alpha}^{2}$ is equal to ______.
34751.sol:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x}y = x{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation.

Here $I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\cos^{2}2x}{2} + cos2x\right) - cos2x}$

$= 2\sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}2xdx}{2 + \tan^{2}2x}$

Put $tan2x = t$

$I = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{tan2x}{\sqrt{2}}$

$∴ IF = {e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{tan2x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)} = {e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

So general solution will be

$y{e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)} = ∫ x{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}{e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}dx$

$y{e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)} = e\dfrac{\pi}{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) + c$

$y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{32} ⇒ c = 0$

i.e. $y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

Given $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\alpha}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\alpha} = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$$= \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)}$

Hence $\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} ⇒ 3{\alpha}^{2} = 2$

34831.text: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = 2x + {x}^{2}tanx, x \in \left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ such that $y\left(0\right) = 1 .$ Then
34831.sol:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = 2x + {x}^{2}tanx$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P = tanx \text{ and } Q = 2x + {x}^{2}tanx$

Now, the integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ tanxdx}$

$= {e}^{lnsecx} = secx$

And, the general solution is $y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$y ⋅ secx = ∫ \left(2x + {x}^{2}tanx\right)secxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + ∫ {x}^{2}\left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)dx + c$

Using integration by parts in the second integral, we get

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + {x}^{2} ∫ \left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)dx - ∫ \left(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({x}^{2}\right) ∫ \left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + {x}^{2} ∫ secxdx - ∫ 2xsecxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = {x}^{2}secx + c$

$⇒ y = {x}^{2} + c \cdot cosx$

Now, $y\left(0\right) = 1$

$⇒ 0 + c = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

So, $y = {x}^{2} + cosx$

Hence, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Differentiating $y ( x )$ with respect to $x$

$⇒ {y}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2x - sinx$

Hence, ${y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and ${y}^{'}\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ {y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - {y}^{'}\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \pi - \sqrt{2} .$

35954.sol:
The cofactor matrix of $A$ is calculated as follows:

$C_{11} = 15$, $C_{12} = -10$, $C_{13} = 8$

$C_{21} = 3$, $C_{22} = 5\alpha$, $C_{23} = -4\alpha$

$C_{31} = -6$, $C_{32} = 4$, $C_{33} = 3\alpha - 2$

The adjoint of $A$ is the transpose of the cofactor matrix:

$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 5\alpha & 4 \\ 8 & -4\alpha & 3\alpha - 2 \end{bmatrix}$

The matrix $B$ is given by:

$B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 4\alpha & -2\alpha \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 5\alpha & 4 \\ 8 & -4\alpha & 3\alpha - 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 16 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 0 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & \alpha - 2 \end{bmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant of $B$ along the second column:

$\det(B) = -3 \begin{vmatrix} -10 & 4 \\ 8 & \alpha - 2 \end{vmatrix} = -3(-10(\alpha - 2) - 32) = -3(-10\alpha - 12) = 30\alpha + 36$

Given $\det(B) = 66$, we get:

$30\alpha + 36 = 66 \Rightarrow 30\alpha = 30 \Rightarrow \alpha = 1$

The determinant of $A$ is:

$\det(A) = \alpha(15 - 0) - 1(10 - 0) + 2(8 - 0) = 15\alpha + 6$

Substituting $\alpha = 1$:

$\det(A) = 15(1) + 6 = 21$

Using the property $\det(\text{adj}(A)) = (\det(A))^{n-1}$ for a $3 \times 3$ matrix:

$\det(\text{adj}(A)) = (\det(A))^2 = (21)^2 = 441$

Answer: $441$

36902.text: The number of pairs $\left(a, b\right)$ of real numbers, such that whenever $\alpha$ is a root of the equation ${x}^{2} + ax + b = 0, {\alpha}^{2} - 2$ is also a root of this equation, is :
36902.sol:
Consider the equation ${x}^{2} + ax + b = 0$

It has two roots (not necessarily real $\alpha$ and $ eta$)

Either $\alpha = eta$ or $\alpha e eta$

Case (1) If $\alpha = eta$, then it is repeated root. Given than ${\alpha}^{2} - 2$ is also root

So, $\alpha = {\alpha}^{2} - 2$

$⇒ \left(\alpha + 1 ight)\left(\alpha - 2 ight) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = - 1$ or $\alpha = 2$

When $\alpha = - 1$ then $\left(a, b ight) = \left(2, 1 ight)$

$\alpha = 2$ then $\left(a, b ight) = \left(- 4, 4 ight)$

Case (2) If $\alpha e eta$, then four possibilities are there

(I) $\alpha = {\alpha}^{2} - 2$ and $ eta = { eta}^{2} - 2$

Here $\left(\alpha, eta ight) = \left(2, - 1 ight)$ or $\left(- 1, 2 ight)$

Hence $\left(a, b ight) = \left(- \left(\alpha + eta ight), \alpha eta ight)$

$= \left(- 1, - 2 ight)$

(II) $\alpha = { eta}^{2} - 2$ and $ eta = {\alpha}^{2} - 2$

Then $\alpha - eta = { eta}^{2} - {\alpha}^{2} = \left( eta - \alpha ight)\left( eta + \alpha ight)$

Since $\alpha e eta$ we get $\alpha + eta = { eta}^{2} + {\alpha}^{2} - 4$

$\alpha + eta = {\left(\alpha + eta ight)}^{2} - 2\alpha eta - 4$

Thus $- 1 = 1 - 2\alpha eta - 4$ which implies

$\alpha eta = - 1$. Therefore $\left(a, b ight) = \left(- \left(\alpha + eta ight), \alpha eta ight)$

$= \left(1, - 1 ight)$

(III) $\alpha = {\alpha}^{2} - 2 = { eta}^{2} - 2$ and $\alpha e eta$

$⇒ \alpha = - eta$

Thus $\alpha = 2, eta = - 2$

$\alpha = - 1, eta = 1$

Therefore $\left(a, b ight) = \left(0, - 4 ight)$ and $\left(0, - 1 ight)$

(IV) $ eta = {\alpha}^{2} - 2 = { eta}^{2} - 2$ and $\alpha e eta$ is same as (III)

Therefore we get $6$ pairs of $\left(a, b ight)$

Which are $\left(2, 1 ight), \left(- 4, 4 ight), \left(- 1, - 2 ight), \left(1, - 1 ight), \left(0, - 4 ight), \left(0, - 1 ight)$

Intersection of $2x + y = 0 \text{ and } x - y = 3$ is $A\left(1, - 2\right)$

Perpendicular bisector of $AB$ is $y - 3 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - 2\right) ⇒ x - 2y + 4 = 0$

Take image of $A$ along the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, we get

$\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + 2}{- 2} = \dfrac{- 2\left(9\right)}{5} = - \dfrac{18}{5}$

i.e. $x = - \dfrac{13}{5}, y = \dfrac{26}{5}$

$B\left(- \dfrac{13}{5}, \dfrac{26}{5}\right)$

This point lies on the line $x + py = 39$

i.e. $- \dfrac{13}{5} + p\left(\dfrac{26}{5}\right) = 39 ⇒ - 1 + 2p = 15$

$⇒ p = 8$

Solving $x + 8y = 39$ and $x - y = 3$, we get $C\left(7, 4\right)$

Now ${\left(AC\right)}^{2} = {\left(1 - 7\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 2 - 4\right)}^{2} = 72 = 9p$

and $A{C}^{2} + {p}^{2} = 72 + 64 = 136$

Also $\DeltaABC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}1 & - 2 & 1 \\ 7 & 4 & 1 \\ \dfrac{- 13}{5} & \dfrac{26}{5} & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[18 + 18 \times \dfrac{13}{5}\right]$

$= 9\left[\dfrac{18}{5}\right] = \dfrac{162}{5} = 32 . 4 \notin \left(34, 38\right)$

38314.text: Let the set of all $a \in R$ such that the equation $cos2x + asinx = 2a - 7$ has a solution be $[ p, q ]$ and $r = tan9 ° - tan27 ° - \dfrac{1}{cot63 °} + tan81 °$, then $pqr$ is equal to ________.
38314.sol:
Given: $cos2x + a \cdot sinx = 2a - 7$

$⇒ 1 - 2\sin^{2}x + a \times sinx = 2a - 7$

$⇒ a \times sinx - 2a = - 8 + 2\sin^{2}x$

$⇒ a\left(sinx - 2\right) = 2\left(\sin^{2}x - 4\right)$

$⇒ a ( sinx - 2 ) = 2 ( sinx - 2 ) ( sinx + 2 )$

$⇒ sinx = 2\left[\text{Not possible}\right], a = 2 ( sinx + 2 )$

We know that, $- 1 \le sinx \le 1$

$⇒ a \in [ 2, 6 ]$

$⇒ p = 2, q = 6$

Now, $r = tan{9}^{°} + cot{9}^{°} - tan{27}^{°} - cot{27}^{°}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{\cos^{2}{9}^{°} + \sin^{2}{9}^{°}}{sin{9}^{°} \cdot cos{9}^{°}} - \dfrac{\cos^{2}{27}^{°} + \sin^{2}{27}^{°}}{sin{27}^{°} \cdot cos{27}^{°}}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1}{sin{9}^{°} \cdot cos{9}^{°}} - \dfrac{1}{sin{27}^{°} \cdot cos{27}^{°}}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{2}{2 \times sin{9}^{°} \cdot cos{9}^{°}} - \dfrac{2}{2 \times sin{27}^{°} \cdot cos{27}^{°}}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{2}{sin{18}^{°}} - \dfrac{2}{sin{54}^{°}}$

$⇒ r = 2\left[\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5} - 1} - \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5} + 1}\right]$

$⇒ r = 8\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{5} + 1 - \sqrt{5} + 1}{5 - 1}\right]$

$⇒ r = 8\left(\dfrac{2}{4}\right)$

$⇒ r = 4$

$⇒ p \cdot q \cdot r = 2 \times 6 \times 4$

$⇒ p \cdot q \cdot r = 48$

39305.text: A nucleus disintegrates into two smaller parts, which have their velocities in the ratio $3: 2$. The ratio of their nuclear sizes will be $\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$. The value of ‘$x$’ is:
39305.sol:
Given here, $\dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Using conservation of momentum during disintegration, we have

${m}_{1}{v}_{1} = {m}_{2}{v}_{2} ⇒ \dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Since, $m = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}ρ$

We have $m ∝ {R}^{3}\left(∵ \text{nuclear mass density}, ρ = \text{constant}\right)$

$\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = {\left(\dfrac{{R}_{1}}{{R}_{2}}\right)}^{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{R}_{1}}{{R}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

So, $x = 2$.

39630.text: Equivalent resistance between the adjacent corners of a regular $n$-sided polygon of uniform wire of resistance $R$ would be :
39630.sol:
Given the total resistance of the wire is $R$. If the polygon has $n$ numbers of side, then the resistance $\left(r\right)$, as shown in the following figure, of each side can be written as

$r = \dfrac{R}{n} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Among all the resistances, $\left(n - 1\right)$ resistances are connected in series combination, whereas, their equivalent resistance is connected in parallel with the ${n}^{th}$ resistance. The equivalent circuit diagram for the above set of resistances can be depicted as follows:

From the above equivalent circuit diagram, the net equivalent resistance $\left({R}_{eq}\right)$ for the entire combination can be calculated as follows-

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} & = & \dfrac{1}{\left(n - 1\right)r} + \dfrac{1}{r} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{\left(n - 1\right)\dfrac{R}{n}} + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{R}{n}} \\ & = & \dfrac{n}{\left(n - 1\right)R} + \dfrac{n}{R} \\ & = & \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{\left(n - 1\right)R} \\ {R}_{eq} & = & \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)R}{{n}^{2}}\end{cases}$

40269.text: A monochromatic source of light operating at $15$ kW emits $2.5\times 10^{22}$ photons/s. The region of an electromagnetic spectrum to which the emitted electromagnetic radiation belongs to ________. (Take $h=6.6\times 10^{-34}$ J·s and $c=3\times 10^8$ m/s).
40269.sol:
Power of the source, $P = 15 \text{ kW} = 15 \times 10^3 \text{ J/s}$

Number of photons emitted per second, $n = 2.5 \times 10^{22} \text{ s}^{-1}$

Energy of one photon, $E = \dfrac{P}{n} = \dfrac{15 \times 10^3}{2.5 \times 10^{22}} = 6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$

Using $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, we get $\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{E}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{6 \times 10^{-19}} = 3.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 330 \text{ nm}$

The wavelength $330 \text{ nm}$ lies in the ultraviolet region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Answer: Ultraviolet

42668.subject: Physics
42668.text: Using a simple pendulum experiment $g$ is determind by measuring its time period $T$. Which of the following plots represent the correct relation between the pendulum length $L$ and time period $T$ ?
42668.sol:
The time period $T$ of a simple pendulum of length $L$ is given by the formula:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$
Squaring both sides, we get:
$T^2 = 4\pi^2 \frac{L}{g}$
Rearranging the equation to find the relationship between $\frac{1}{T^2}$ and $L$:
$\frac{1}{T^2} = \frac{g}{4\pi^2 L}$
Let $y = \frac{1}{T^2}$ and $x = L$. The equation becomes:
$y = \frac{k}{x}$ where $k = \frac{g}{4\pi^2}$ is a constant.
This is the equation of a rectangular hyperbola in the first quadrant.
As $L$ increases, $\frac{1}{T^2}$ decreases non-linearly, approaching the axes asymptotically.
Comparing this with the given plots, option (2) correctly represents a hyperbolic relationship between $\frac{1}{T^2}$ and $L$.

46935.text: Organs which differ in origin but perform similar functions :
46935.sol:
The organs which have similar function but are different in their structure and origin are called analogous organs.
The organs which have same fundamental structure and origin but function may be similar or different, are called homologous organs.
The organs which are present in reduced form and do not correspond to the fully developed functional organs to related animals are called vestigial organs.

47258.subject: Biology
47258.text: Identify the incorrect statement regarding respiratory system in man.
options: Lungs are covered by double-layered membrane called pleura.
The alveoli are surrounded by rich blood capillaries.
The trachea, bronchi and bronchioles are supported by 'O' shaped cartilaginous rings.
The right lung is slightly larger than the left lung.
47258.sol:
The trachea, primary, secondary and tertiary bronchi, and initial bronchioles are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings, which are 'C' shaped, not 'O' shaped. These incomplete rings prevent the collapse of the airway during breathing.

The lungs are covered by a double-layered pleural membrane which reduces friction on the lung surface.

The alveoli are highly vascularised and surrounded by a rich network of blood capillaries for efficient gaseous exchange.

The right lung is slightly larger and heavier than the left lung, as the left lung contains a cardiac notch to accommodate the heart.

Answer: The trachea, bronchi and bronchioles are supported by 'O' shaped cartilaginous rings.

47307.text:
$\xrightarrow{\large{\text{Conc.HNO}_3/\text{Conc.H}_2\text{SO}_4,\ 323-333\text{K}}} A \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Fe/HCl}}} B \xrightarrow{\large{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl},\ 273\text{K}}} C \xrightarrow{\large{\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH},\ -\text{N}_2}}+ D + \text{HCl}$

Organic compound 'D' is
47307.sol:
Benzene undergoes nitration with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $323-333\text{ K}$ to form nitrobenzene (A).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Conc. HNO}_3 / \text{Conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2 \text{ (A)}$

Nitrobenzene (A) is reduced by $\text{Fe/HCl}$ to yield aniline (B).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Fe/HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \text{ (B)}$

Aniline (B) undergoes diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $273\text{ K}$ to form benzene diazonium chloride (C).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl},\ 273\text{K}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \text{ (C)}$

Benzene diazonium chloride (C) is reduced by ethanol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) to benzene. In this process, ethanol acts as a reducing agent and gets oxidized to acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{N}_2 + \text{HCl}$

Therefore, the organic compound D is acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$

50102.subject: Physics
50102.text: What will be the total electric flux through the faces of the cube as given in the figure with side of length '$a$' if a charge Q is placed at B midpoint of an edge of the cube (see figure)?
50102.sol:
According to Gauss's Law, the total electric flux through a closed surface is given by $\Phi = \dfrac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}$.

The charge $Q$ is placed at the midpoint of an edge of the cube. This charge is not completely enclosed by the single cube. To completely enclose the charge symmetrically, we can imagine placing three additional identical cubes such that all four cubes share this common edge.

The total charge enclosed by this larger Gaussian surface (made of 4 cubes) is $Q$. Therefore, the total electric flux through the combination of these 4 cubes is $\dfrac{Q}{\varepsilon_0}$.

By symmetry, the flux is shared equally among the 4 cubes. Thus, the total electric flux passing through the faces of the given single cube is:
$\Phi_{\text{cube}} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{Q}{\varepsilon_0} = \dfrac{Q}{4\varepsilon_0}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Q}{4\varepsilon_0}$

54858.text: Which of following on oxidation forms propanone?
54858.sol:
Oxidation of secondary alcohols yields ketones.

2-Propanol is a secondary alcohol containing three carbon atoms. Upon oxidation with common oxidizing agents like acidic $K_2Cr_2O_7$ or $KMnO_4$, it forms propanone (acetone).

$CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3 \xrightarrow{[O]} CH_3-CO-CH_3 + H_2O$

1-Propanol is a primary alcohol and oxidizes to propanal, which further oxidizes to propanoic acid.

2-Butanol oxidizes to 2-butanone.

2-methylbu\tan^{-1}-ol oxidizes to 2-methylbutanoic acid.

Answer: 2-Propanol

55139.subject: Chemistry
55139.text: Which of the following does NOT exhibit haloform reaction?
55139.sol:
Haloform Reaction Analysis

Compounds exhibiting the haloform reaction contain the methyl ketone group $CH_3CO-$ or are oxidizable to this structure (e.g., $CH_3CH(OH)R$).

Ethanal (CH_3CHO$) contains the $CH_3CO-$ moiety and undergoes haloform reaction.

Propanone (CH_3COCH_3$) is a methyl ketone with two $CH_3CO-$ groups and exhibits the reaction.

Butanone (CH_3COCH_2CH_3$) contains the $CH_3CO-$ moiety and undergoes haloform reaction.

Propanal (CH_3CH_2CHO$) lacks the $CH_3CO-$ moiety, possessing instead $CH_3CH_2CO-$, and does not exhibit the haloform reaction.

The compound that does not undergo haloform reaction is therefore $\boxed{B}$.

55149.subject: Chemistry
55149.text: Which from following compounds has highest boiling point?
55149.sol:
Boiling points in organic compounds are governed by intermolecular force strength. Among homologous aldehyde series, increasing molecular weight and chain length enhance London dispersion interactions.

Molecular weights are calculated as follows: acetaldehyde (C_{2}H_{4}O) $\mathrm{MW}=44.06$ g/mol, propionaldehyde (C_{3}H_{6}O) $\mathrm{MW}=58.09$ g/mol, butyraldehyde (C_{4}H_{8}O) $\mathrm{MW}=72.12$ g/mol, and valeraldehyde (C_{5}H_{10}O) $\mathrm{MW}=86.15$ g/mol.

Valeraldehyde possesses the greatest molecular mass and longest carbon chain, resulting in the most substantial London dispersion forces. These stronger interactions necessitate higher energy input for phase transition, correlating with an elevated boiling point.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

55656.subject: Chemistry
55656.text: Identify the product obtained when isopropyl magnesium chloride in dry ether reacts with dry ice forming a complex, hydrolysed further.
55656.sol:
Isopropyl magnesium chloride is $(CH_3)_2CHMgCl$.

Dry ice is solid $CO_2$.

When a Grignard reagent reacts with dry ice, it undergoes nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group of $CO_2$ to form a magnesium carboxylate complex.

$(CH_3)_2CHMgCl + O=C=O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-COOMgCl$

Upon acid hydrolysis, the complex yields a carboxylic acid.

$(CH_3)_2CH-COOMgCl + H_2O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-COOH + Mg(OH)Cl$

The product $(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$ is 2-methylpropanoic acid.

Answer: 2 - Methylpropanoic acid

56429.subject: Chemistry
56429.text: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ ?
options: It is $sp^3 d^2$ hybridised and tetrahedral.
It is $d^2 sp^3$ hybridised and octahedral.
It is $dsp^2$ hybridised and square planar
It is $sp^3 d^2$ hybridised and octahedral.
56429.sol:
The given complex is $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$.

Let the oxidation state of Mn be $x$.

$x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$

The electronic configuration of Mn is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals against Hund's rule. The four electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, leaving two $e_g$ orbitals empty.

These two empty $3d$ orbitals, along with one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, undergo $d^2sp^3$ hybridization.

The geometry corresponding to $d^2sp^3$ hybridization is octahedral.

Answer: It is $d^2 sp^3$ hybridised and octahedral.

57182.text: Which from following is a non benzenoid aromatic compound?
57182.sol:
Non-benzenoid aromatic compounds satisfy Hückel's rule while lacking a benzene ring structure.

Aniline contains a benzene ring, making it benzenoid aromatic.

Naphthalene consists of fused benzene rings, classifying it as benzenoid aromatic.

Phenol features a benzene ring substituent, rendering it benzenoid aromatic.

Tropone forms a seven-membered cycloheptatrienone ring with $6\pi$ electrons satisfying Hückel's rule (4n + 2$ where $n = 1$), establishing it as non-benzenoid aromatic.

The non-benzenoid aromatic compound is therefore \boxed{B}$.

59861.subject: Chemistry
59861.text: Calculate the change in internal energy if an ideal gas expands from $0.5\ \text{dm}^3$ to $3.5\ \text{dm}^3$ at constant pressure 2 bar by absorbing 1800 J heat energy.
59861.sol:
Given $V_1 = 0.5\ \text{dm}^3$, $V_2 = 3.5\ \text{dm}^3$, $P = 2\ \text{bar}$, and heat absorbed $q = 1800\ \text{J}$.

Work done during expansion at constant pressure is given by $W = -P(V_2 - V_1)$.

$W = -2 \times (3.5 - 0.5) = -6\ \text{bar}\cdot\text{dm}^3$

Since $1\ \text{bar}\cdot\text{dm}^3 = 100\ \text{J}$, we have $W = -600\ \text{J}$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + W$.

Substituting the values, $\Delta U = 1800 - 600 = 1200\ \text{J}$.

Answer: $1200$ J.

59862.subject: Chemistry
59862.text: The enthalpy of combustion of C, $\text{H}_2$, and $\text{CH}_4$ are $-390$, $-285$ and $-890$ kJ/mol. Find the enthalpy of formation of methane.
59862.sol:
The required reaction for the formation of methane is:

$\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_4\text{(g)}$

The enthalpy of formation can be calculated using the enthalpies of combustion of the reactants and products:

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = \Delta H_c(\text{C}) + 2\Delta H_c(\text{H}_2) - \Delta H_c(\text{CH}_4)$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -390 + 2(-285) - (-890)$

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -390 - 570 + 890$

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -960 + 890 = -70 \text{ kJ/mol}$

Answer: $-70$ kJ

60827.subject: Mathematics
60827.text: If $(1 + i) \cdot (1 + 2i) \ldots\ldots\ldots (1 + ni) = x + iy$ (Where $i = \sqrt{-1}$ ), then the value of $(2) \cdot (5) \cdot (10)\ldots\ldots\ldots(1 + n^2)$
60827.sol:
Given $(1 + i)(1 + 2i) \dots (1 + ni) = x + iy$

Taking the conjugate on both sides:

$(1 - i)(1 - 2i) \dots (1 - ni) = x - iy$

Multiplying the two equations:

$((1 + i)(1 - i))((1 + 2i)(1 - 2i)) \dots ((1 + ni)(1 - ni)) = (x + iy)(x - iy)$

$(1^2 - i^2)(1^2 - (2i)^2) \dots (1^2 - (ni)^2) = x^2 - (iy)^2$

Since $i^2 = -1$, we get:

$(1 + 1)(1 + 4) \dots (1 + n^2) = x^2 + y^2$

$2 \cdot 5 \cdot 10 \dots (1 + n^2) = x^2 + y^2$

Answer: $x^2 + y^2$

61437.text: If a body is heated to $110^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and placed in air at $10^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ after 1 hour its temperature is $60^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$, then the additional time required for it to cool to $30^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is

$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{d} T}{\mathrm{ d} t}=-K(T-10) \\
& \Rightarrow T-10=e^{-k t+C} \\
& \Rightarrow T=10+e^C \cdot e^{-k t}
\end{aligned}$
For $t=0$,
$\begin{aligned}
& T=110 \\
& \Rightarrow e^C=100 \text{ i.e. } \\
& T=10+100 \cdot e^{-k t}
\end{aligned}$
For $t=1$,
$\begin{aligned}
& T=60 \\
& \Rightarrow 60=10+100 \cdot e^{-k \times 1} \\
& \Rightarrow-k=\log \frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow k=\log 2
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow T=10+100 \cdot e^{-\left(\log _2\right) t}$
Putting $T=30\begin{aligned}
& 30=10+100 \cdot e^{-\left(\log _2\right) t} \\
& \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{1}{5}\right)=-(\log 2) t \\
& \Rightarrow t=\frac{\log 5}{\log 2}
\end{aligned}$
Additional time $=t-1=\frac{\log 5}{log2}-1$

61638.subject: Mathematics
61638.text: The derivative of $\log_{10} x$ with respect to $\log_x 10$ is
61638.sol:
Let $u = \log_{10} x$ and $v = \log_x 10$.

Using the base change property of logarithms, $v = \dfrac{1}{\log_{10} x} = \dfrac{1}{u}$.

Differentiating $v$ with respect to $u$, we get $\dfrac{dv}{du} = -\dfrac{1}{u^2}$.

The derivative of $u$ with respect to $v$ is given by $\dfrac{du}{dv} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{dv}{du}}$.

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{dv}{du}$, we get $\dfrac{du}{dv} = -u^2$.

Replacing $u$ with $\log_{10} x$, we obtain $\dfrac{du}{dv} = -(\log_{10} x)^2$.

Answer: $-(\log_{10} x)^2$

62932.text: The statement pattern $[(p \wedge q) \rightarrow (\sim p \vee r)] \vee [(\sim p \vee r) \rightarrow (p \wedge q)]$ is
62932.sol:
Let $A = p \wedge q$ and $B = \sim p \vee r$.

The given statement pattern can be written as $(A \rightarrow B) \vee (B \rightarrow A)$.

Using the logical equivalence $X \rightarrow Y \equiv \sim X \vee Y$, the expression becomes:

$(\sim A \vee B) \vee (\sim B \vee A)$

Using the commutative and associative properties of disjunction, we can rearrange the terms as:

$(\sim A \vee A) \vee (\sim B \vee B)$

We know that for any statement $X$, $\sim X \vee X \equiv T$ (where $T$ represents a tautology).

Substituting this into the expression, we get:

$T \vee T \equiv T$

Therefore, the given statement pattern is a tautology.

Answer: a tautology

63976.subject: Mathematics
63976.text:
In a triangle $A B C$, with usual notations.
$\frac{2 \cos A}{a}+\frac{\cos B}{b}+\frac{2 \cos C}{c}=\frac{a}{b c}+\frac{b}{c a}$
Then $\angle \mathrm{A}=$
63976.sol:
Given the equation:

$\frac{2 \cos A}{a} + \frac{\cos B}{b} + \frac{2 \cos C}{c} = \frac{a}{b c} + \frac{b}{c a}$

Apply the cosine rule to express trigonometric terms:

$\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2 b c}, \quad \cos B = \frac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2}{2 a c}, \quad \cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2 a b}$

Substitute into the left-hand side:

$\begin{align*}\text{LHS}$&= $\frac{2}{a} \cdot \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2 b c} + \frac{1}{b} \cdot \frac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2}{2 a c} + \frac{2}{c} \cdot \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2 a b}$\\ &= $\frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{a b c} + \frac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2}{2 a b c} + \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{a b c} \end{align*}$

Combine terms over a common denominator of $2 a b c$:

$\frac{2(b^2 + c^2 - a^2) + (a^2 + c^2 - b^2) + 2(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)}{2 a b c}$

Simplify the numerator:

$2b^2 + 2c^2 - 2a^2 + a^2 + c^2 - b^2 + 2a^2 + 2b^2 - 2c^2 = a^2 + 3b^2 + c^2$

Thus, $\text{LHS} = \frac{a^2 + 3b^2 + c^2}{2 a b c}$

The right-hand side simplifies to:

$\frac{a}{b c} + \frac{b}{c a} = \frac{a^2 + b^2}{a b c}$

Equating both sides:

$\frac{a^2 + 3b^2 + c^2}{2 a b c} = \frac{a^2 + b^2}{a b c}$

Multiply through by $2 a b c$:

$a^2 + 3b^2 + c^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2)$

Simplify:

$a^2 + 3b^2 + c^2 = 2a^2 + 2b^2 \Rightarrow b^2 + c^2 = a^2$

This is a Pythagorean relation, indicating that angle $A$ is a right angle.

Conclusion: $\angle A = 90^{}^{\circ} = \frac{\pi}{2}$

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

64067.subject: Mathematics
64067.text: Let $a$ be an integer selected at random from the set $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$. The probability that the equation $ax^2 - ax + 1 = 0$ has real roots is...
64067.sol:
The total number of possible values for $a$ from the set $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$ is $10$.

For the equation $ax^2 - ax + 1 = 0$ to have real roots, we consider two cases:

If $a = 0$, the equation becomes $1 = 0$, which has no roots.

If $a \neq 0$, the equation is a quadratic equation. For it to have real roots, its discriminant must be non-negative.

$D = (-a)^2 - 4(a)(1) \geq 0$

$a^2 - 4a \geq 0$

$a(a - 4) \geq 0$

Since $a \in \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$, the condition $a(a - 4) \geq 0$ is satisfied when $a \geq 4$.

The favorable values of $a$ are $4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9$.

The number of favorable outcomes is $6$.

The required probability is $\dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{5}$

64200.text: The line $L_1$ given by $\dfrac{x}{p} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$ passes through the point $(5,0)$. The line $L_2$ given by $\dfrac{x}{10} + \dfrac{y}{q} = 1$ is parallel to $L_1$. Then the distance between the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ is...
64200.sol:
Since the line $L_1$ given by $\dfrac{x}{p} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$ passes through $(5,0)$, substituting these coordinates gives:

$\dfrac{5}{p} + 0 = 1 \Rightarrow p = 5$

The equation of $L_1$ becomes $\dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$, which simplifies to $2x + 5y - 10 = 0$.

The line $L_2$ given by $\dfrac{x}{10} + \dfrac{y}{q} = 1$ is parallel to $L_1$. Equating their slopes:

$-\dfrac{q}{10} = -\dfrac{2}{5} \Rightarrow q = 4$

The equation of $L_2$ becomes $\dfrac{x}{10} + \dfrac{y}{4} = 1$, which simplifies to $4x + 10y - 40 = 0$ or $2x + 5y - 20 = 0$.

The perpendicular distance between the parallel lines $2x + 5y - 10 = 0$ and $2x + 5y - 20 = 0$ is:

$d = \dfrac{|-10 - (-20)|}{\sqrt{2^2 + 5^2}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{4 + 25}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{29}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{29}}$

65593.subject: Physics
65593.text: In series LCR circuit R $=18 \Omega$ and impedance is $30 \Omega$. An rms voltage 210 V is applied across the circuit. The true power consumed in AC circuit is nearly
65593.sol:
Given a series LCR circuit with resistance $R = 18 \, \Omega$, impedance $Z = 30 \, \Omega$, and RMS voltage $V_{\text{rms}} = 210 \, \text{V}$, the RMS current is determined by Ohm's law:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} = \frac{210}{30} = 7 \, \text{A}$.

The true power in a resistive component is given by $P = I_{\text{rms}^2 R$, yielding:

$P = (7)^2 \times 18 = 49 \times 18 = 882 \, \text{W}$.

This result is confirmed by the alternative expression $P = \frac{V_{\text{rms}^2 R}{Z^2}$, which evaluates to $\frac{210^2 \times 18}{30^2} = \frac{44100 \times 18}{900} = 882 \, \text{W}$.

The calculated power of $882 \, \text{W}$ is closest to the option $900 \, \text{W}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{900 W}}$

67397.text: The average force applied on the walls of a closed container depends on temperature (T) as (T is the temperature of an ideal gas)
67397.sol:
For an ideal gas in a closed container, the volume $V$ and the number of moles $n$ are constant.

Using the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$.

Since $V$, $n$, and $R$ are constants, the pressure $P$ is directly proportional to the absolute temperature $T$, i.e., $P \propto T$.

The average force $F$ exerted by the gas on the walls of the container is given by $F = P \times A$, where $A$ is the surface area of the walls.

Since the container is closed and rigid, the area $A$ is constant.

Therefore, $F \propto P \propto T$.

The average force depends on temperature as $T^1$.

Answer: $T^1$

70192.text: In a single slit diffraction pattern, the distance between the plane of the slit and screen is 1.3 m. The width of the slit is 0.65 mm and the second maximum is formed at the distance of 2.6 mm from the centre of the screen. The wavelength of light used is
70192.sol:
Single-slit diffraction secondary maxima satisfy $a \sin \theta_m = \left(m + \frac{1}{2}\right)\lambda$ for $m = 1, 2, 3, \dots$, where $a$ is the slit width and $\lambda$ the wavelength.

For the second maximum (m = 2$) at small angle \theta_2$, $\sin \theta_2 \approx y_2/D$ where $y_2 = 2.6 \times 10^{-3}$ m is the fringe position and $D = 1.3$ m the slit-to-screen distance.

Substituting $a = 0.65 \times 10^{-3}$ m gives:

$a \frac{y_2}{D} = \frac{5}{2}\lambda$

Solving for $\lambda$:

$\lambda = \frac{2}{5} \cdot \frac{(0.65 \times 10^{-3}) \cdot (2.6 \times 10^{-3})}{1.3}$

Calculating yields $\lambda = 0.52 \times 10^{-6}$ m.

Converting to Ångstroms (1$ Å $= 10^{-10}$ m):

\lambda = 0.52 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{10} = 5200$ Å

The wavelength is therefore $\boxed{5200 \text{ Å}}$.

71032.sol:
Ecological succession is the gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area.

During succession, some species colonise an area and their populations become more numerous, whereas populations of other species decline and even disappear.

The entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area are called sere(s).

The individual transitional communities are termed seral stages or seral communities.

Answer: The entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area

71370.subject: Biology
71370.text: In a population with two alleles B and b with frequency $0.6$ and $0.4$ in Hardy-Weinberg equillibrium. How many heterozygous individuals in a sample of $250$ can be expected?
71370.sol:
According to the Hardy-Weinberg principle, the frequency of alleles in a population is represented by $p$ and $q$.

Given the frequency of allele B is $p = 0.6$ and the frequency of allele b is $q = 0.4$.

The frequency of heterozygous individuals is given by $2pq$.

$2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$

The expected number of heterozygous individuals in a sample of $250$ is $2pq \times 250$.

$0.48 \times 250 = 120$

Answer: $120$

72321.subject: Physics
72321.text: $Two particles A and B execute S.H.M.s of periods T and \dfrac{5T}{2}$. If they start from the mean position, then the phase difference between them when the particle A completes two oscillations will be (in radian)
72321.sol:
Time taken by particle A to complete two oscillations is $t = 2T$.

The phase of a particle executing S.H.M. starting from the mean position at time $t$ is given by $\phi = \omega t = \dfrac{2\pi}{T'}t$, where $T'$ is the time period.

For particle A, the phase at $t = 2T$ is:
$\phi_A = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \times 2T = 4\pi$

For particle B, the time period is $T_B = \dfrac{5T}{2}$. The phase at $t = 2T$ is:
$\phi_B = \dfrac{2\pi}{\dfrac{5T}{2}} \times 2T = \dfrac{4\pi}{5T} \times 2T = \dfrac{8\pi}{5}$

The phase difference between the two particles is:
$\Delta\phi = \phi_A - \phi_B = 4\pi - \dfrac{8\pi}{5} = \dfrac{12\pi}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{12\pi}{5}$

72579.subject: General Ability
72579.text:
Read the following pairs:
Active VoicePassive Voice
They laughed at his warnings and objected to all his proposals.His warnings were laughed at and his proposals were objected to.
Do not insult the weak.You are advised to not insult the weak.

Select the pair(s) wherein the Passive Voice is correctly stated.
72579.sol:
In the first pair, the active voice contains prepositional verbs, laughed at and objected to. When converting such sentences to the passive voice, the prepositions must remain attached to the verbs. The given passive sentence correctly retains these prepositions. Thus, the first pair represents a correct transformation.

In the second pair, the active voice is an imperative sentence in the negative form. When converting a negative imperative sentence to the passive voice using introductory verbs like advised, the standard grammatical structure requires the use of not to followed by the base verb. The given passive sentence incorrectly uses a split infinitive, to not insult. The correct passive form should be You are advised not to insult the weak, or alternatively, Let the weak not be insulted. Thus, the second pair is incorrect.

Therefore, only the first pair states the passive voice correctly.

Answer: I only

72629.text:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. In many countries, there are millions of people who are underprivileged and deprived
S6. In the past forced labour was imposed by landlords, money-lenders, and other wealthy persons
P. Both of these are prohibited under the Constitution of India

R. The marginalised are often subjected to exploitation by their fellow human beings
S. Another closely related form of exploitation is buying and selling of human beings and using them as slaves
72629.sol:
The first sentence S1 introduces the underprivileged and deprived people. Sentence R logically follows S1 by referring to these people as 'The marginalised' and introduces the concept of 'exploitation'.

Sentence Q follows R as it gives an example of the exploitation mentioned in R ('One such form of exploitation').

Sentence S follows Q by providing a second example ('Another closely related form of exploitation').

Sentence P refers back to the two forms of exploitation mentioned in Q and S using the phrase 'Both of these'.

Finally, S6 provides historical context to the forced labour mentioned in Q and prohibited in P. Thus, the correct logical sequence is R Q S P.

Answer: R Q S P

75360.subject: General Ability
75360.text:
Which of the following statements in respect of landslides are correct?
1. These occur only on gentle slopes during rain.
2. They generally occur in clay-rich soil.
3. Earthquakes trigger landslides.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75360.sol: A landslide is defined as the movement of a mass of rock, debris, or earth down a slope. Landslides are a type of "mass wasting," which denotes any down-slope movement of soil and rock under the direct influence of gravity. Slope movement occurs when forces acting down-slope (mainly due to gravity) exceed the strength of the earth materials that compose the slope. Causes include factors that increase the effects of down-slope forces and factors that contribute to low or reduced strength. Landslides can be initiated in slopes already on the verge of movement by rainfall, snowmelt, changes in water level, stream erosion, changes in ground water, earthquakes, volcanic activity, disturbance by human activities, or any combination of these factors. Earthquake shaking and other factors can also induce landslides underwater. These landslides are called submarine landslides. Submarine landslides sometimes cause tsunamis that damage coastal areas.

78004.text: $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ are three mutually exclusive and exhaustive events associated with a random experiment. If $3 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=4 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})$ and $3 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})=2 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})$, then what is $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})$ equal to?
78004.sol:
Given that $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive events
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{ A})+\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{ B})+\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})=1$....(i)
Given $3 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=4 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})$ ....(ii)
and $3 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})=2 \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})$.....(iii)
Put (ii) and (iii) in (i), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{3}{4} P(B)+P(B)+\frac{2}{3} P(B)=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{9 P(B)+12 P(B)+8 P(B)}{12}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{29 P(B)}{12}=1 \Rightarrow P(B)=\frac{12}{29}
\end{aligned}$
Put the value of $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})$ in (ii), we get
$\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{ A})=\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{ B})=\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{12}{29}=\frac{9}{29}$

85582.subject: Biology
85582.text:
Bacteria have cell wall made of a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid connected by $\beta$-1,4 glycosidic bonds. Lysozyme, an enzyme, cleaves the glycosidic bond and disrupts the cell wall structure.

In an experiment, Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, which differ in terms of cell envelope and peptidoglycan thickness, are treated with lysozyme and subsequently placed in a hypotonic solution. The correct statement about the effect of the treatment is:
options: Gram-positive bacteria are lysed, but not Gram-negative bacteria.
Both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria are lysed.
Neither Gram-positive nor Gram-negative bacteria are lysed.
85582.sol:
Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer that is directly exposed to the external environment. Lysozyme easily accesses and cleaves the $\beta$-1,4 glycosidic bonds in their peptidoglycan, destroying the cell wall. When these cells are subsequently placed in a hypotonic solution, water enters the cells due to endosmosis, causing them to swell and lyse.

Gram-negative bacteria possess an outer membrane composed of lipopolysaccharides and proteins that surrounds their thin peptidoglycan layer. This outer membrane acts as a permeability barrier, preventing lysozyme from reaching the peptidoglycan. Consequently, their cell wall remains intact, and they do not lyse in a hypotonic solution.

Thus, Gram-positive bacteria are lysed, but Gram-negative bacteria are not.

Answer: Gram-positive bacteria are lysed, but not Gram-negative bacteria.

86885.subject: Physics
86885.text: An incandescent lamp of wattage $W$ is filled with argon gas and has a tungsten filament. The collision frequency of evaporated tungsten atoms with the argon atoms is found to be proportional to $W^\alpha$. The most reasonable value of $\alpha$ is
86885.sol:
According to the Stefan-Boltzmann law, the power or wattage $W$ radiated by the tungsten filament is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature $T$:

$W \propto T^4 \Rightarrow T \propto W^{1/4}$

The collision frequency $f$ of an evaporated tungsten atom with argon atoms in the bulb is given by the kinetic theory of gases:

$f = \sqrt{2} \pi d^2 n v_{rel}$

Since the bulb is a sealed container, the volume is constant, meaning the number density $n$ of argon atoms remains constant. The mean relative speed $v_{rel}$ of the atoms is proportional to the square root of the temperature:

$v_{rel} \propto \sqrt{T}$

Therefore, the collision frequency $f$ is proportional to $\sqrt{T}$:

$f \propto \sqrt{T}$

Substituting $T \propto W^{1/4}$ into the above relation, we get:

$f \propto \sqrt{W^{1/4}} = W^{1/8}$

Comparing this with $f \propto W^\alpha$, we find the most reasonable value of $\alpha$ is $\dfrac{1}{8}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{8}$

90302.sol:
For function $f\left(x\right)$ at $x = 0$
L.H.L. $= \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}f\left(0 - h\right) = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{{2}^{- \dfrac{1}{h}} - 1}{{2}^{- \dfrac{1}{h}} + 1}$$= \dfrac{0 - 1}{0 + 1} = - 1$
R.H.L. $= \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}f\left(0 + h\right) = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{{2}^{\dfrac{1}{h}} - 1}{{2}^{\dfrac{1}{h}} + 1} = \lim_{h \to 0 +}\dfrac{1 - {2}^{- \dfrac{1}{h}}}{1 + {2}^{- \dfrac{1}{h}}}$$= \dfrac{1 - 0}{1 + 0} = 1$
Since, $\lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}f\left(0 - h\right) \ne \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}f\left(0 - h\right),$

therefore, $f\left(x\right)$ is not continuous and not differentiable at $x = 0 .$

91786.text: If $\mathop{\text{Σ}}_{\text{k} = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{\left(\text{k} + 2\right)\sqrt{\text{k}} + \text{k}\sqrt{\text{k} + 2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\text{a}} + \sqrt{\text{b}}}{\sqrt{\text{c}}}$, where $a, b, c \in N$ and $a, b, c \in [ 1, 15 ]$, then $a + b + c$ is equal to
91786.sol:
Here, general term ${T}_{k} = \dfrac{1}{( k + 2 )\sqrt{k} + k\sqrt{k + 2}}$

Rationalising the expression, we get,

$⇒$ ${\text{T}}_{\text{k}} = \dfrac{\left(\text{k} + 2\right) \sqrt{\text{k}} - \text{k} \sqrt{\text{k} + 2}}{\text{k} {\left(\text{k} + 2\right)}^{2} - {\text{k}}^{2} \left(\text{k} + 2\right)}$

$⇒ {T}_{k} = \dfrac{( k + 2 )\sqrt{k} - k\sqrt{k + 2}}{2k( k + 2 )} = \dfrac{1}{2}( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k + 2}} )$

Now, ${T}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} ),$

${T}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4}} ),$

${\text{T}}_{3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right]$ and so on

${T}_{k} = \dfrac{1}{2}( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k + 2}} )$

Adding all the terms, we get,

${T}_{1} + {T}_{2} + . .. {T}_{k} = \dfrac{1}{2}( 1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k + 1}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k + 2}} )$

Now, if $k \to \infty$

$\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}{T}_{k} = \dfrac{1}{2}( 1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - 0 - 0 )$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{1} + \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$\dfrac{\sqrt{1} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{8}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{4}}{\sqrt{16}}$

As, $c \in [ 1, 15 ] ⇒ c = 8, a = 1, b = 2$

$⇒$ any other solution is not possible

$⇒ a + b + c = 11$

In a transformer the primary and secondary currents are related by

${I}_{s} = \left(\dfrac{{N}_{p}}{{N}_{s}}\right){I}_{p}$

And the voltage are related by

${V}_{s} = \left(\dfrac{{N}_{s}}{{N}_{p}}\right){V}_{p}$

Where subscripts p and s refer to the primary and secondary of the transformer.

Here, ${V}_{p} = V, \dfrac{{N}_{p}}{{N}_{s}} = 4$

$∴ {I}_{s} = 4{I}_{p}$

And ${V}_{s} = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)V = \dfrac{V}{4}$

95315.subject: Botany
95315.text: Which of the following options CORRECTLY shows the sequence of different tissues of the periderm starting from the periphery?
95315.sol: The cylindrical tissue that forms the protective covering of stems and roots during the early secondary growth of perennial plants is known as periderm. They are seen only in plants that show secondary growth and these tissues replace the epidermis of the same plant. Phellem or the cork is present in the outer cortical cells and prevents the rupturing of the outer tissues. Phellogen is the cork cambium and is found on the side of the phellem. Phelloderm is the secondary cortex which is produced in the inner side of the phellogen.

100356.subject: Physics
100356.text: A motorcyclist is travelling due East at $10\text{ m/s}$. They take a turn due North and simultaneously increase their speed to $10\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}$. The angle that the average force acting on the motorcyclist makes with the West direction is :
100356.sol:
Taking East as the positive x-axis ($\hat{i}$) and North as the positive y-axis ($\hat{j}$):
Initial velocity, $\vec{v}_i = 10\hat{i}$
Final velocity, $\vec{v}_f = 10\sqrt{3}\hat{j}$

According to Newton's second law, the average force acts in the direction of the change in velocity ($\Delta\vec{v}$):
$\Delta\vec{v} = \vec{v}_f - \vec{v}_i = -10\hat{i} + 10\sqrt{3}\hat{j}$

This vector has a negative x-component (West) and a positive y-component (North), so it lies in the North-West quadrant.
The angle $\theta$ it makes with the West direction (negative x-axis) is given by:
$\tan\theta = \dfrac{|\text{y-component}|}{|\text{x-component}|} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{10} = \sqrt{3}$

Thus, $\theta = 60^{\circ}$.
The average force is directed $60^{\circ}$ North of West.

Answer: $60^{\circ}$ North of West

105680.sol:
From conservation of energy the kinetic energy of electron equals the maximum photon energy (we neglect the work function $\phi$ because it is normally so small compared to $e V_0$ ).
$\therefore \quad e V_0=h v_{\max }$ or $e V_0=\frac{h c}{\lambda_{\min }} \therefore \quad V_0=\frac{h c}{e \lambda_{\min }}
or \begin{aligned} V_0 & =\frac{12400 \times 10^{-10}}{10^{-11}} \\ & =124 \mathrm{kV}\end{aligned}$
Hence, accelerating voltage for electrons in $X$-ray machine should be less than 124 kV .

108528.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Enthalpy of neutralization of reaction.
\(\mathrm{HF}+\mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NaF}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \text{ is }-16.7 \mathrm{Kcal} / \text{ eq. }\)
Reason (R) : HF is a strong acid so, its enthalpy of neutralization increases with strong base.

options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
108528.sol:
- Assertion (A): The enthalpy of neutralization for the reaction \(\mathrm{HF}+\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaF}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) is indeed approximately \(-16.7 \mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{eq}\). This value indicates that the reaction is exothermic, which is correct.
- Reason (R): HF is a weak acid, not a strong acid. Therefore, the assertion that the enthalpy of neutralization increases with a strong base when a strong acid is involved is misleading. The enthalpy of neutralization for weak acids tends to be less negative compared to strong acids. Hence, while the assertion is correct, the reason is incorrect.

114907.subject: Chemistry
114907.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a first-order reaction, the time taken for $99\%$ completion is exactly twice the time taken for $90\%$ completion.

Reason (R): The time required for the completion of a given fraction of a first-order reaction is independent of its initial concentration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
114907.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the time required for a specific percentage of completion is given by $t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\dfrac{a_0}{a_0 - x}\right)$.

For $90\%$ completion:
$t_{90\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\dfrac{100}{100 - 90}\right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log(10) = \dfrac{2.303}{k}$

For $99\%$ completion:
$t_{99\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\dfrac{100}{100 - 99}\right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log(100) = 2 \times \dfrac{2.303}{k}$

Therefore, $t_{99\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%}$. Assertion (A) is true.

Reason (R) states that the time for fractional completion is independent of initial concentration, which is a true characteristic of first-order kinetics. However, this fact does not explain why $t_{99\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%}$. The factor of 2 arises from the properties of logarithms ($\log 10^2 = 2 \log 10$), not merely from the independence of initial concentration. Thus, both statements are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

114911.subject: Chemistry
114911.text:
The decomposition of ammonia on a platinum surface is a zero-order reaction:

$2\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g})$

If the initial concentration of $\text{NH}_3$ is $0.5$ M and the rate of appearance of $\text{H}_2$ is $6.0 \times 10^{-3}$ M min$^{-1}$, what will be the concentration of $\text{NH}_3$ remaining after $40$ minutes?
114911.sol:
For the zero-order reaction $2\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$, the rate of reaction is:

$\text{Rate} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\text{NH}_3]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{d[\text{H}_2]}{dt} = k$

Given the rate of appearance of $\text{H}_2$ is $6.0 \times 10^{-3}$ M min$^{-1}$:
$\dfrac{d[\text{H}_2]}{dt} = 3k = 6.0 \times 10^{-3}$ M min$^{-1}$
$\Rightarrow k = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}$ M min$^{-1}$

The rate of disappearance of $\text{NH}_3$ is:
$-\dfrac{d[\text{NH}_3]}{dt} = 2k = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}$ M min$^{-1}$

Using the integrated rate law for the disappearance of $\text{NH}_3$:
$[\text{NH}_3]_0 - [\text{NH}_3]_t = 2kt$

Substitute the given values ($[\text{NH}_3]_0 = 0.5$ M, $t = 40$ min):
$0.5 - [\text{NH}_3]_t = (4.0 \times 10^{-3}) \times 40$
$0.5 - [\text{NH}_3]_t = 0.16$

$[\text{NH}_3]_t = 0.5 - 0.16 = 0.34$ M

The concentration of $\text{NH}_3$ remaining is $0.34$ M.

Answer: $0.34$ M

117778.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the crystal field electronic configuration of the central metal ion.

List-I (Complex Ion)List-II (Electronic Configuration)
(A) $[Cr(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$(I) $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$
(B) $[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$(II) $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$
(C) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$(III) $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$
(D) $[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$(IV) $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
117778.sol:
(A) $[Cr(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$: Cr is in +3 oxidation state. The electronic configuration is $d^3$. For a $d^3$ ion in an octahedral field, the configuration is always $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$ regardless of ligand strength. (Matches III)

(B) $[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$: Mn is in +2 oxidation state. The electronic configuration is $d^5$. $H_2O$ is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$), so it forms a high-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. (Matches I)

(C) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$: Fe is in +3 oxidation state. The electronic configuration is $d^5$. $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand ($\Delta_o > P$), so it forms a low-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$. (Matches IV)

(D) $[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$: Ni is in +2 oxidation state. The electronic configuration is $d^8$. For a $d^8$ ion in an octahedral field, the configuration is always $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$ regardless of ligand strength. (Matches II)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

117810.subject: Chemistry
117810.text:
Consider the coordination complex $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ and the following statements regarding its properties:
(I) It is an inner orbital complex.
(II) Its spin-only magnetic moment is approximately $4.90 \text{ BM}$.
(III) Its crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) is $-0.4 \Delta_{\text{o}}$.
(IV) It is a diamagnetic complex.

How many of the above statements are correct?
117810.sol:
The given complex is $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$. The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$, which has a $3\text{d}^{6}$ electronic configuration.

Since $\text{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, pairing of electrons does not occur prior to filling of $\text{e}_{\text{g}}$ orbitals ($\Delta_{\text{o}} < \text{P}$). The complex is high-spin with the configuration $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$.

Statement (I) is incorrect: It uses outer $4\text{d}$ orbitals for hybridization ($\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$), making it an outer orbital complex.

Statement (II) is correct: With 4 unpaired electrons ($n=4$), the spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90 \text{ BM}$.

Statement (III) is correct: CFSE = $(-0.4 \times n_{\text{t}_{2\text{g}}} + 0.6 \times n_{\text{e}_{\text{g}}})\Delta_{\text{o}} = (-0.4 \times 4 + 0.6 \times 2)\Delta_{\text{o}} = -0.4 \Delta_{\text{o}}$.

Statement (IV) is incorrect: Due to the presence of unpaired electrons, it is a paramagnetic complex.

Thus, exactly 2 statements are correct.

Answer: 2

123844.subject: Botany
123844.text: A student observes a meiotic cell where the nucleolus has disappeared and the nuclear envelope has completely broken down. This stage is immediately preceded by a specific phase of Prophase-I. Which of the following events is the primary characteristic of this preceding phase?
123844.sol:
The disappearance of the nucleolus and the breakdown of the nuclear envelope mark the end of diakinesis, the final stage of Prophase-I.

The stage that immediately precedes diakinesis is diplotene.

The primary characteristic of the diplotene stage is the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata.

Terminalisation of chiasmata occurs in diakinesis, appearance of recombination nodules occurs in pachytene, and the formation of the synaptonemal complex occurs in zygotene.

Answer: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex

125300.subject: Botany
125300.text: What transformation is involved in photosynthesis?
125300.sol: All animals including human beings depend on plants for their food. Have you ever wondered from where plants get their food? Green plants, in fact, have to make or rather synthesise the food they need and all other organisms depend on them for their needs. The green plants make or rather synthesise the food they need through photosynthesis and are therefore called autotrophs. You have already learnt that the autotrophic nutrition is found only in plants and all other organisms that depend on the green plants for food are heterotrophs. Green plants carry out ‘photosynthesis’, a physico-chemical process by which they use light energy to drive the synthesis of organic compounds. Ultimately, all living forms on earth depend on sunlight for energy.The use of energy from sunlight by plants doing photosynthesis is the basis of life on earth. Photosynthesis is important due to two reasons: it is the primary source of all food on earth. It is also responsible for the release of oxygen into the atmosphere by green plants. This chapter focuses on the structure of the photosynthetic machinery and the various reactions that transform light energy into chemical energy.

125442.text: What type of leaf anatomy do C4 plants have?
125442.sol: The particularly large cells around the vascular bundles of the C4 plants are called bundle sheath cells, and the leaves which have such anatomy are said to have ‘Kranz’ anatomy. ‘Kranz’ means ‘wreath’ and is a reflection of the arrangement of cells. The bundle sheath cells may form several layers around the vascular bundles; they are characterised by having a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. You may like to cut a section of the leaves of C4 plants – maize or sorghum – to observe the Kranz anatomy and the distribution of mesophyll cells.

125676.subject: Botany
125676.text: A researcher adds a chemical agent to an isolated chloroplast suspension that makes the thylakoid membrane highly permeable to protons. If this suspension is exposed to light, which of the following processes will be immediately inhibited?
options: Absorption of light energy by photosystems
125676.sol:
According to the chemiosmotic hypothesis, the synthesis of ATP is strictly dependent on the creation and maintenance of a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane. If a chemical agent makes the membrane highly permeable to protons, the protons will simply diffuse back into the stroma without passing through the ATP synthase enzyme ($CF_0$-$CF_1$ complex). Consequently, no proton gradient can be established, and ATP synthesis will be immediately inhibited.

The absorption of light, splitting of water, and electron transport leading to the synthesis of NADPH are driven by light and electron flow. They do not directly require the proton gradient, so they will not be immediately stopped by this chemical agent.

Answer: Synthesis of ATP

125911.subject: Botany
125911.text: What is the effect of having both male and female flowers on the same plant, such as in castor and maize?
options: It prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy
It prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy
It synchronizes pollen release and stigma receptivity
125911.sol: Outbreeding Devices: Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. Both these devices prevent autogamy. The third device to prevent inbreeding is self-incompatibility. This is a genetic mechanism and prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil. Another device to prevent self-pollination is the production of unisexual flowers. If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as castor and maize (monoecious), it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy. In several species such as papaya, male and female flowers are present on different plants, that is each plant is either male or female (dioecy). This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.

126276.subject: Botany
126276.text: In a typical angiosperm, if the chromosome number in the endosperm is $72$, what will be the chromosome number in its synergid cell and secondary nucleus, respectively?
126276.sol:
The endosperm of a typical angiosperm is a triploid ($3n$) tissue formed by triple fusion.

Given the endosperm chromosome number is $72$, we have $3n = 72$, which means the haploid chromosome number is $n = 24$.

The synergid is a cell of the female gametophyte (embryo sac) and is haploid ($n$). Therefore, its chromosome number is $24$.

The secondary nucleus is formed by the fusion of two haploid polar nuclei in the central cell before fertilization, making it diploid ($2n$). Therefore, its chromosome number is $2 \times 24 = 48$.

Thus, the chromosome numbers are $24$ and $48$, respectively.

Answer: $24$ and $48$

126309.subject: Botany
126309.text:
Assertion : Colpa aurea is a specialised pollinating agent of orchid Ophrys speculum.
Reason : Male Colpa mistakes the Ophrys flower for female wasp to copulate with it.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
126309.sol: For its pollination, the orchid Ophrys speculum has picked the most selective attraction in the entire animal kingdom. It is pollinated by a hairy wasp, Colpa aurea. The wasp has a fixed habit whereby its males leave the burrows for above ground existence about four weeks before the females emerge for the open air mating. The orchid opens its flowers about the same time the males appear and they possess an appearance and odour similar to those possessed by the female wasp. The inexperienced males mistake the Ophrys flowers for their female counterparts and land to perform the act of pseudocopulation. The insect repeats the act with a number of orchid flowers and carries pollinia from one flower to another thereby affecting pollination in the orchid.

127247.subject: Botany
options: Protecting endangered species in their natural habitat
Protective maintenance in zoological parks and botanical gardens
127247.sol: Biodiversity conservation may be in situ as well as ex situ. In in situ conservation, the endangered species are protected in their natural habitat so that the entire ecosystem is protected. Recently, 34 ‘biodiversity hotspots’ in the world have been proposed for intensive conservation efforts. Of these, three (Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Himalaya and Indo-Burma) cover India’s rich biodiversity regions. Our country’s in situ conservation efforts are reflected in its 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, > 450 wildlife sanctuaries and many sacred groves. Ex situ conservation methods include protective maintenance of threatened species in zoological parks and botanical gardens, in vitro fertilisation, tissue culture propagation and cryopreservation of gametes.

Reason (R): The number of species waiting to be saved from extinction far exceeds the conservation resources available due to the conflict between development and conservation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
127384.sol:
According to NCERT, faced with the conflict between development and conservation, many nations find it unrealistic and economically not feasible to conserve all their biological wealth. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

Invariably, the number of species waiting to be saved from extinction far exceeds the conservation resources available. This makes Reason (R) a true statement.

Hence, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true
